reviews.title: Subscription and AI
reviews.text: Steal your content to train their AI and charge you to do it.  No thanks.

reviews.title: So many issues
reviews.text: I wanted to like this app so much. I have been back and forth with support for weeks and it’s like talking to a wall. Contacts do not populate when sending emails, not even in forwarded emails with one of the people in copy. The worse part is the notification badges. They would show 34 emails, when you open the app there’s like 3, without reading any of them once you exit the app there’s badge is gone completely. This is just using @icloud email, no subscription either, I wanted to test basic functionality before subscribing, this can’t even do that. The response from support is to check all email clients and make sure there are no unread emails… the only other client I have emails forwarded from is Gmail and that’s pretty ridiculous I would need to constantly check Gmail for unread mail. They asked if this happened in my home only due to firewall, antivirus etc., this happens everywhere, cellular service, other WiFi’s as well.

reviews.title: Support is Atrocious
reviews.text: Sadly, I’ve given the Spark team plenty of opportunities to respond to me (which they initially did on X) but they have since gone dark without any follow up on the ticket they said would create. This is not only unacceptable but ultimately disappointing. I pay for this service, have used them for nearly 10 years as my email client and even explained to them that if they weren’t going to get back to me, that I’d have to resort to leaving a negative review…well here I am. I have ALWAYS had issues with using my working App Specific Password (required by Apple) to connect my iCloud account when upgrading to a new phone. Every year. This year I finally reached out to ask why, as I have to create a new ASP and then log into EACH of my 4 devices every single time. Other apps have no issue with my ASP, only Spark. I would NOT recommend this app and suggest you take your email business elsewhere.

reviews.title: Infuriating automation. Not a serious app.
reviews.text:
It makes videos much bigger when it prepares them to be attached to an email, then tells you they're too big to send and to upgrade to use Spark Cloud.

First, don't change my videos.
Second, both my provider and the recipient's allow attachments up to 50MB, and that's pretty standard, so why is this app putting a lower limit on?

iOS Mail has mandatory compression (again, why?) but at least I can send something, even if it's degraded. This is just a blocker to getting anything done. Joke of an email app.

On top of this, updates periodically reset your signature options, adding a "Sent with Spark [hyperlink]" note to the bottom of new emails. Getting caught by this when you're trying to send a quick reply leaves a bitter taste.

And as if that's not all too much already, when you install Spark on an additional device, it resets many of your settings (e.g groups) and syncs them through iCloud to all your other devices.

Never before have I encountered an app that is so disrespectful of user choices.

I've now abandoned the app since it can't even handle a follow-up to a reply without messing up the chain. Replying to your last reply to get an answer? That doesn't work.

I will not miss this app. It has massive ridiculous issues everywhere.

If it doesn’t download the emails at all then I have to go to gmail and see them and they open fine. After spending several days and one entire day trying to fix the issue on my end I’ve given up. There’s no point in paying for another email app, especially if it’s not working. And I don’t believe the customer should have to go down 50 rabbit holes and it still doesn’t fix the problem. There are a lot of features I liked and that was why I was willing to pay for it. I might consider reinstalling it if I can be assured that it’s been fixed, if not…it’s been nice knowing you. reviews.title: Pushing AI is really annoying
reviews.text:
I originally switched to Spark because Gmail was forcibly integrating Gemini into everything and it was obnoxious. Spark was a welcome alternative - I felt like I could just have an email client that wasn’t constantly trying to sell me things. Well, now they’re also pushing their own AI offerings through the mobile app - desktop is still usable and I like it, but the mobile app is absolutely ridden with sales pitches. Not to mention, it now glitches regularly - I was just drafting an email and out of nowhere, it returned an error message that the draft was deleted. This happens regularly. I was willing to look past the periodic issues because not having AI shoved down my throat was worth it to me, but now, there’s no point for me to be using it. 

I wish these companies and designers would configure their offerings in a way that allowed you to truly opt out of AI. If someone wants to use it, great, I love that for them. But if these companies were to do that, they may discover that no one actually wants any of this garbage. It’s bloatware. It’s a waste of resources. It does not live up to its inflated expectations. And that would be a tough pill to swallow.

Anyway, deleting it, bye!

reviews.title: Email notification count still doesn’t work
reviews.text:
I left a review several years ago stating that there were issues with the badge count displaying an incorrect number of unread emails. This has been better on and off since then but has never been completely fixed. The app icon will show 7 unread messages; I open the app and there are really only 2 unread messages. The app icon will then update to show 2 unread messages, only to change later, again showing an incorrect number. I thought maybe this had something to do with the mail server. However, none of my other mail apps have this issue. Maybe the developers can explain what’s going on. Could be something I can fix on my end.

UPDATE: Can’t believe this badge count bug is still happening years later. Right now, my Spark icon badge count shows 13 unread messages. In actuality, there are zero unread messages. This seems to be an inherent bug that’s been around from the beginning of Spark. Sure wish they’d fix it.
